title: Traceability Between Test Basis and Test Work Products
concept:
**Traceability** is the ability to identify related items, such as requirements, test conditions, test cases, test results, and defects. Good traceability supports many testing activities:

**Impact analysis** — when a requirement changes, traceability identifies the test cases that must be updated or re-run.

**Coverage measurement** — comparing the set of requirements to the set of test cases that exercise them shows what is and is not tested.

**Audit and compliance** — regulated domains (medical, aerospace, automotive) demand documented evidence that every requirement was tested.

**Defect investigation** — if a test fails, traceability quickly identifies the requirement it covers and helps prioritise the fix.

**Test reporting** — traceability allows reports to be aggregated by feature, requirement, or risk.

In practice, traceability is maintained using identifiers and tooling: every requirement has an ID; each test case references the requirement IDs it covers; each defect references the failing test case. Tools (ALM, Jira with plugins, Polarion) automate the linkage.
keyPoints: Traceability links test basis (requirements, designs) to test conditions, test cases, results, and defects.
It supports impact analysis, coverage measurement, audit, defect investigation, and meaningful reporting.
Maintained via stable IDs and ALM tooling that records the relationships between artifacts.

quiz.question: A regulator requests evidence that every requirement in version 2.0 was tested. Which testware property is MOST critical for satisfying this request?
options: Traceability between requirements and test cases.
Code coverage percentage of the AUT.
quiz.explanation: Traceability is the property that lets you demonstrate, requirement-by-requirement, which test cases exercise it and what the latest results were. Execution speed, automation counts, and code coverage are useful but do not by themselves answer 'is every requirement tested?'
